non_goals: The remaining ten Refusal write sites (#1010-#1013). This slice settles that the FIRST one lands here, and ships that one only.
The policy_gate_held lane's 22-member AutoApprovalBlockReason map, its precedence order and its veto set — #1013 writes that lane and #1013 carries its vocabulary.
The five lane maps this slice does not write (held_draft, auto_post_revoked, ask_withheld, outreach_withheld, batch_halted), the refusalCategoryFor resolver, and REFUSAL_CATEGORY_META's owner labels.
The Restraint tab, any read path over refusal_events, and any owner-facing surface (#1014).
Any migration. Migration 116 is already applied to staging and production; this slice adds no SQL file.
Backfilling any Refusal decided before the ledger existed — #1002 ruled no backfill, ever.
RENDER_WITHHOLD_REASONS from the parked branch. #1002 killed read.ts, and that constant existed only for read.ts's timestamp partition.

Re-testing migration 116's five CHECK constraints or its partial-index idempotency. #1008 already proves both, including C1's fall-through, in src/lib/shared/__tests__/migration-116-refusal-events.integration.test.ts.

Reworking AutonomyGovernorScheduler's per-candidate containment. The amendment adds a Sentry sink inside its EXISTING catch block; the catch itself, the cursor advance and the loop stay exactly as they are.
user_visible_behavior: No owner-visible change. Nothing reads refusal_events until #1014.
An autonomy suspension writes exactly one refusal_events row per account, alongside the account_audit_log row it already writes, in the same transaction.
Setting REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED=false stops every ledger write without a deploy; suspension, audit and notification behaviour are byte-identical to today.
The ArchivalPoller 'Archived' log line carries a refusal_events count, and refusal_events joins the saturation list.
A failure anywhere inside a Governor suspension candidate now raises a Sentry issue instead of reaching the structured log alone.
invariants: The ledger must never break the thing it records: a duplicate subject is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, never a raised error that aborts the deciding transaction.
The ON CONFLICT clause re-spells refusal_events_subject_uniq's predicate byte-for-byte — WHERE subject_id IS NOT NULL — because Postgres cannot infer a partial index otherwise.
occurredAt is required and never optional. Date | 'transaction_time'; an omission must be a type error, not a silent drift to insert time.
No site reads transaction_timestamp() and passes it back as a JS Date — postgres.js truncates microseconds on decode (#520).

autonomy_suspended writes business_id IS NULL, subject_type NULL and subject_id NULL. One row per account, never one per location — this is the parent effort's defect and CHECK C3 makes it unrepresentable.
REFUSAL_SOURCES, REFUSAL_CATEGORIES and REFUSAL_SUBJECT_TYPES mirror migration 116's CHECK members exactly. A partial TypeScript union would be a second authority that drifts.

WriteRefusalEventInput is a per-lane union transcribing CHECKs C1-C4, so an illegal lane/subject/code pairing cannot be written. It is a compile-time PROJECTION of migration 116, never a replacement — every CHECK stays in the SQL, and refusalCategory is deliberately NOT narrowed per lane because #1001 declined to pin a lane's category.
REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED is server-authoritative with no NEXT_PUBLIC companion (invariant #13), read live per call via readFlagEnabledByDefault.
The helper takes tx: TransactionSql as an explicit parameter and never imports @/lib/db/server (invariant #15).
The retention sweep is deliberately cross-tenant and carries its tenant-scope allowlist exemption; without it ci:tenant-scope fails.
Tenant isolation: every refusal_events row carries account_id NOT NULL, and the table keeps deny-all RLS.

A ledger failure aborts the deciding transaction and is never swallowed inside the helper. Telemetry around it IS swallowed — observability must never poison the path it observes, and that applies to EVERY telemetry call this change adds, including the one added inside AutonomyGovernorScheduler's containment catch.

The kill-switch warning is rate-limited per DISABLED EPISODE, never per process: the latch clears when the helper next observes the flag enabled, so a second outage in one process still warns. The DURABLE signal is the structured log line, emitted first and outside the Sentry guard — Sentry's captureMessage returns on queue rather than on delivery and swallows transport failures internally, so no latch on it can detect a real delivery failure and none may claim to.
Every test this branch adds executes. No .todo, no .skip, no .fails — the gate's promised-tests row matches titles only, so an inert eval passes it.
edge_cases: Kill switch off: the helper returns without touching the deciding transaction, and emits one warning per DISABLED EPISODE — the ledger structurally cannot show its own gap.
Kill switch off mid-process: the flag is read live per call, so a toggle takes effect without a restart, in both directions.
Sentry itself throws while the kill switch is off: the helper still returns cleanly and the suspension is unaffected. Telemetry may not poison the disabled path.

Sentry throws ONCE and then recovers: the warning still reaches Sentry on a later call. Setting the latch before the attempt would trade one network blip for silence for the rest of that disabled episode.

Sentry throws MANY times and then recovers: the warning still arrives, and the durable log line landed on every attempt regardless. A lifetime attempt ceiling would be exhausted by then, which is why the retry is a time-based cooldown rather than a counter.
Sentry accepts the capture and then fails in transport: the log line is the signal. captureMessage cannot report this, so the code does not pretend to retry it.
The flag is disabled a SECOND time in one process: it warns again. Rate limiting is per disabled episode, not per process lifetime.

A lane is paired with a subject its CHECK forbids: this is a COMPILE error, not a 23514. WriteRefusalEventInput is a per-lane union transcribing C1-C4, and adding a lane to REFUSAL_SOURCES without an arm fails to compile.

Every test title is present AND active. A .todo test satisfies the gate's promised-tests row while executing nothing, so test 26's scan runs at MODULE SCOPE — vitest loads the module even when the test is marked, which is what makes the check independent of itself.
Sentry throws inside the Governor cycle's containment catch: the cycle still advances to the next candidate. Telemetry added to observe a contained failure must not become an uncontained one.
Two suspensions of one account: both persist as two Refusals, because the partial unique index excludes a NULL subject_id.
suspendAccountAutonomy returns newlySuspended: false (the policy was already suspended): no ledger row is written, because no decision was made.

A CHECK violation from a writer bug still aborts the decision transaction, rolling back the policy row, the audit row and the notice outbox rows together. ON CONFLICT covers duplicate keys only. The kill switch is the lever, and it is not a revert deploy.

That abort inside the Governor cycle is contained to one candidate by design; the cycle advances its cursor and continues. It must raise a Sentry issue, or the account stays un-suspended silently on every 15-minute cycle.
The ArchivalPoller arm shares the ten existing arms' single try/catch, so its SQL must be valid against a promoted 116 — which it is, since 116 is applied to staging and production.
The sweep's ORDER BY (occurred_at, id) must match idx_refusal_events_archival, or the sweep is unbounded.
The sweep keys on occurred_at and never on created_at. A row whose two clocks disagree must be swept by the decision clock alone.
Rows exactly at the 180-day boundary: the arm uses a strict < comparison, matching the nine sibling arms.

rollback_plan: Three layers, in order of reach. (1) Flag flip: REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED=false on Railway stops every ledger write with no deploy, and leaves suspension, audit and notification behaviour byte-identical to today; invoke the flag-flip skill. (2) PR revert on main plus a redeploy — this removes the helper, the caller, the poller arm and the scheduler's Sentry sink together. (3) NO down migration and no migration 117. Migration 116 stays: it is already applied to staging and production, it is immutability-guarded, and an empty table with no writer is inert. Rows already written are NOT deleted by a rollback, and layer 2 REMOVES THE SWEEP THAT WOULD RETIRE THEM: the ArchivalPoller arm reverts with the PR, so surviving rows then have no writer, no reader and no pruner and sit until a later slice restores the arm. That is acceptable — the table is empty of readers and #1002 forbids any backfill — but it must not be described as self-cleaning, which an earlier draft of this field wrongly did. If retiring them matters, delete them explicitly at revert time; do not wait for a sweep that the revert just removed.
observability: One warning per DISABLED EPISODE whenever REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED is false and a write is attempted — a structured log line first and always (the durable signal), then a best-effort Sentry capture at level warning. Never per process: the latch clears when the flag is next seen enabled, so a second outage warns again. This is the only signal that the ledger has a gap, because the ledger cannot show its own absence. NEITHER transport pages anyone today — no Sentry alert rule keys on subsystem:refusal_ledger, and beta-launch-alerting.md records that no route is configured yet; that gap is pre-existing and shared with every warning-level capture in the repo.

A ledger failure has TWO callers and they reach Sentry by DIFFERENT routes, which is why the amendment exists. JudgeWorker is a BullMQ worker, so attachJobFailureSink raises an issue on the terminal attempt. AutonomyGovernorScheduler is NOT a BullMQ worker — it is a guarded poll whose per-candidate catch emitted logger.error alone, so a ledger failure there would have left the account un-suspended silently on every 15-minute cycle. This slice adds the Sentry capture inside that existing catch.
The ArchivalPoller 'Archived' log line carries a refusal_events count, and the batch-limit warning names refusal_events when a cycle saturates at 5000.

Reconciliation query that proves the lane works in production: COUNT(*) of refusal_events WHERE refusal_source = 'autonomy_suspended' must equal COUNT(*) of account_audit_log WHERE event_type = 'autonomy_suspended', per account, over a window STRICTLY INSIDE the last REFUSAL_LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS. Past day 180 the two counts diverge BY DESIGN and the query means nothing: ArchivalPoller sweeps refusal_events on occurred_at, and account_audit_log has no archival arm at all, so the audit side keeps rows the ledger has correctly retired. Inside the window a divergence means either the flag is off or a write is failing. It is prose, not a shipped artifact: no poller, route, runbook or alert executes it today.
